items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: I didn't know what it was. I didn't know at that time when I stepped into Small’s it was a new club...

ctx.x: In your bio there’s a brief anecdote about you finally arriving in New York and going to Small’s. And I wonder if that, I can only envision if maybe that was a moment to remember for you — what was that like to sort of step into a club and say okay, this is a big part of the New York scene and how do I fit into this.

Wow that’s a beautiful question because you really brought me back to that moment. I mean the name of the club is called Small’s, which still exists, so I didn’t know what it was. I didn’t know at that time when I stepped into Small’s it was a new club that was encouraging young people to find who they are through the tradition of bebop and hard bop, but open the doors for experiments for people to write their own music and to make their own bands, and I just witnessed a couple of people that I knew, because…

walked into Small’s and he’s — there he was just playing the bass, swinging his butt off, and being part of the scene. And so for me more than thinking of like what is Small’s or the scenes of New York, for me it was kind of the idea that somebody from Israel, from a different country, from where I come from, from my city, can just be part of a whole new culture and mingle so well and excel. So there was a few other Israelis at the time that were part of that scene, so for me it was, and I remember that night I…
